chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Walīd, who said: My father informed me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Sahl, from Zakariyyā ibn Ādam, who said:
I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about the fistula, and he said: “Only three things invalidate wudu (ablution): urine, feces, and wind.”
(19) As for the report narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from the nephew of Fuḍayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
He said regarding a man from whom something like a pumpkin seed comes out: “Wudu (ablution) is upon him.” This is to be understood as when it is smeared with feces.

(20) As indicated by what al-Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked about a man who is in his salat (prayer), and from whom a pumpkin seed comes out—what should he do? He said: “If it comes out clean of feces, then nothing is upon him and his wudu (ablution) is not invalidated. But if it comes out smeared with feces, then he must repeat the wudu (ablution); and if he is in his salat (prayer), he should break the prayer and repeat the wudu (ablution) and the prayer.”

key_terms.اَلرِّيحُ: wind, one of the things that invalidates wudu (ablution)
key_terms.اَلنَّاصُورِ: fistula, a bodily condition asked about in relation to ritual purity
key_terms.اَلْبَوْلُ: urine, one of the things that invalidates wudu (ablution)
key_terms.اَلْعَذِرَةِ: feces, in this context the substance whose presence affects the ruling
key_terms.اَلْغَائِطُ: feces, one of the things that invalidates wudu (ablution)
key_terms.اَلْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before worship
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), the act of worship affected by the purity ruling

ai.seo_question: What things invalidate wudu (ablution) according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام and Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal rulings of ritual purity and what invalidates wudu (ablution). It states that wudu is invalidated by urine, feces, and wind, and it clarifies that the emergence of a solid object only requires wudu if it is contaminated with feces.
